description: A Bot's tasks, a page of the right-hand side panel: scripts the Bot's host keeps and runs (Python, shell, or a prompt the Bot is given as a turn), by hand or as a trigger fires (a schedule, a git push to a branch of a repo on the host), each run given its form filled by hand or by the trigger's event, the Bot asked mid-run when the script can't decide and handed a failed run. The page goes from the list of tasks to a task's page to a run's log, each with a back button. Only exists while the open chat is a Bot; otherwise the tab is hidden, and if it was shown the panel falls back to Meta. docs/tasks-design.md has the model and the wire.
opens: the 'Tasks' tab (alarm-clock icon) in the side panel's switcher, visible only while the open chat is a Bot

parts.name: tab
parts.shows: Switcher tab with an alarm-clock icon and the label 'Tasks'; present only for a Bot chat.

parts.name: list
parts.shows: The first view. A row at the top with empty space at the left and a flat + button at the right (tooltip 'New task'), then a boxed list of the Bot's tasks in the order its host keeps them, scrolling, no selection. Empty: the centred dim text 'No tasks yet'. Read when the chat is opened, when a turn of the Bot ends, every 30 seconds while the page is shown (5 while a run is going), and after each change here.

parts.name: task row
parts.shows: Before the title, its last run's state icon (a tick done, a stop sign failed, a spinner running or asking, a square stopped, an arrow skipped; nothing if it has never run; its state's word as the tooltip). Title: the task's name. At the end: a switch (on = its triggers fire; tooltip 'Turn off to pause') and a Run button (play icon). No subtitle. Row text is escaped, never markup.

actions.does: pauses or resumes its triggers on the host at once (a schedule resumed is worked out afresh from now)
runs it now; a task with form fields opens the run form first

parts.name: task page
parts.shows: A header row: a back button (tooltip 'Tasks'), the task's name in bold (ellipsized), then flat buttons Run (play), Change (pencil) and Delete (trash). Below it, scrolling, four groups each with its heading: 'Triggers', 'Form', 'Script', 'Runs'. Read when opened, every 5 seconds while a run is going, and after each change here.

actions.does: deletes the task on the host (no confirmation) and goes back to the list

parts.name: triggers
parts.shows: Heading 'Triggers' with a flat + at its right (tooltip 'Add trigger'). One row per trigger: an icon (alarm clock for a schedule, branch for a git push), the title saying what fires it ('weekdays at 09:00', 'every 2 hours', 'push to main in ~/site'), a warning icon with the trigger's last error as its tooltip if it has one, and a remove button (minus; tooltip 'Remove trigger'). No triggers: the dim line 'By hand' (every task can be run by hand).

actions.does: removes the trigger on the host at once

parts.name: form
parts.shows: Heading 'Form' with a flat pencil at its right (tooltip 'Change'). One row per field: title its label (or name), at the end its type in dim text (Text, Number, Yes or no, Choice). No fields: the dim line 'No fields'.

parts.name: script
parts.shows: Heading 'Script' with, at its right, how it runs (Python, Shell or Bot) and its version (12 hex, monospace, dim). Under it the script in a code block (highlighted as Python or shell; a Bot task's prompt as plain text).

parts.name: runs
parts.shows: Heading 'Runs'. Its latest runs, newest first: the state icon, the title '<when> · <how long>' (when: HH:MM if today, else 'Mon 03 Nov 14:00', host clock; how long: '12 s' or '3 min 4 s'), and at the end an icon for what started it (play by hand, alarm clock schedule, branch git push) and the version, monospace, dim. A dry run's title ends ' · Dry run'. None: the dim line 'No runs yet'.

parts.name: run page
parts.shows: A header row: a back button (tooltip the task's name), the title '<task> · <when>' in bold, and a Stop button (stop icon) while it's running or asking. Then one line: its state's word, what started it ('By hand', 'Schedule', 'Git push'), how long it took and its version. Then its log, scrolling, in order: the script's output and errors in code blocks (consecutive lines together; errors in the error colour), each line it said as plain text, each ask of the Bot as a card headed 'Asked <Bot>' (or 'Handed to <Bot>' for a failure handed over) with what was asked, each answer as a card headed '<Bot> answered' with the Bot's answer, and the run's state changes as dim lines. Read every second while it's going.

actions.does: stops the run on the host

parts.name: message line
parts.shows: A dim wrapping line at the bottom of the page (10 px margins), hidden unless something failed: "Couldn't load the tasks.", "Couldn't run the task.", "Couldn't save the task.", "Couldn't delete the task.", "Couldn't stop the run."; the host's reason is in its tooltip. It goes away after the next successful answer.

parts.name: task dialog
parts.shows: An alert dialog headed 'New Task' (or 'Change Task'), Cancel and Save (suggested). Content (scrolls, 520 px at most): a 'Name' field; 'Runs as' with a drop-down Python / Shell / Bot; the label 'Script' over a monospace multi-line box (at least 200 px tall); a switch row 'Hand failures to the Bot' (on for a new task).

actions.does: saves it on the host (a new script makes a new version); a new task's page opens

parts.name: run form
parts.shows: An alert dialog headed 'Run <task>' with one control per field: text field, number box, switch, or drop-down of its choices, each labelled, filled with its default; buttons Cancel, Dry run and Run (suggested).

actions.does: runs it with the form as filled
runs it with its asks answered by a dummy agent and its failure not handed to the Bot

parts.name: trigger dialog
parts.shows: An alert dialog headed 'Add Trigger', Cancel and Save. A drop-down Schedule / Git push. Schedule: 'Every' or 'At a time of day'; every: a number and minutes / hours (5 minutes to a month); at: 'Times in <zone>' (or 'Times on the host's clock'), an HH:MM field and seven day toggles Mon to Sun. Git push: 'Repository folder' (a path on the host) and 'Branch' (main). Then, if the task has fields, 'Fills' and one drop-down per field, '<field> from', with 'nothing' and the trigger's payload keys (schedule: time; git push: repo, branch, before, after, commit, message, author), set to the key of the field's own name if there is one.

parts.name: form dialog
parts.shows: An alert dialog headed 'Form', Cancel and Save. One row per field: a name field, a type drop-down (Text, Number, Yes or no, Choice), a 'Choices, comma-separated' field shown for a choice, a 'Default' field, and a remove button (tooltip 'Remove field'); under them an 'Add field' button.

states.name: running
states.shows: A spinner before the task's name and run; the run page's Stop button

states.name: asking
states.shows: As running, its state 'asking its Bot'; the run's log ends with the ask's card

states.name: failed
states.shows: Stop-sign icon; the run's log ends with the error, and a 'Handed to <Bot>' card with the Bot's answer if it was handed over

decisions.said: Routines are rewritten as Tasks: tasks are scripts, run on a schedule or by hand at any time
decisions.rule: Every app shows a Bot's tasks where its routines were, each runnable by hand, with its triggers (a schedule among them)

decisions.said: Triggers generalise schedules; a task can be started by external events, a git push first
decisions.rule: Every app lists a task's triggers (schedule, git push) and adds or removes them on the task's page

decisions.said: A task's script can call its Bot as a fallback on errors and to handle non-deterministic steps
decisions.rule: Every app shows a run's asks of its Bot and the Bot's answers in the run's log, a failure handed over marked so

decisions.said: Input forms that triggers populate, and that the Bot can fill
decisions.rule: Every app shows a task's form, fills it before a run by hand, and lets a trigger map its payload onto the fields

decisions.said: Telemetry includes when triggers happen, how long scripts take, failures and version hashes
decisions.rule: Every app lists a task's runs with when, how long, what started it, how it ended and the version it ran

decisions.said: Test a workflow with a dummy agent and check the format is correct
decisions.rule: Every app's run form offers a Dry run, its asks answered by a dummy agent
